title: Apply to go to court for a fine
summary: You can apply to have a fine matter heard and decided in court if you received a fine notice, reminder notice, or overdue fine.
intro:
If you received a fine (fine notice, fine reminder notice or overdue fine), you can apply to have the matter heard and decided in court.

### When to apply

You need to apply before the due date on your fine reminder notice.

If you paid your fine before the overdue date, you have 90 days from the date the fine was issued to go to court.

If your fine is overdue, see Apply to go to court for an overdue fine.

who_can_apply: The person named on the fine notice.
The vehicle owner if there is no name on the notice.
The authorised representative of the person named on the notice, provided they complete the Authority to Act form.
what_you_need: Your name, date of birth, and driver licence details.
Your residential address (PO boxes are not accepted) to post your Court Attendance Notice (CAN).
For camera-detected seatbelt offences, you must nominate the driver for both driver and passenger fines.

faqs.q: When do I need to apply to go to court?
faqs.a: You must apply before the due date on your fine reminder notice. If you paid your fine before the overdue date, you have 90 days from the date the fine was issued to go to court.

faqs.q: Who can apply to have the fine matter heard in court?
faqs.a: The person named on the fine notice, the vehicle owner (if no name is on the notice), or the authorised representative of the person named on the notice (who must complete the Authority to Act form).

faqs.q: What do I need to apply to go to court?
faqs.a: You need your name, date of birth, driver licence details, residential address (PO boxes are not accepted) for the Court Attendance Notice (CAN), your fine notice number, and the date of the offence.
